name: eino
description:
eino is a cloud platform for designing private wireless networks — indoor and outdoor
Wi-Fi, cellular (4G/5G/CBRS), DAS, and public-safety ERRCS. Design engineers use it to
model buildings and sites, place radios and antennas, simulate RF coverage and capacity,
and produce the reports and bills of materials handed to installers.

This connector gives Claude read-only access to the projects you can already see in eino,
so you can interrogate a design in plain language instead of clicking through panels and
exporting spreadsheets.

What you can ask for:

• Project overview — building, floors, geolocation, and which networks and technologies
  are in use
• Portfolio summary — across every project you own or that has been shared with you
• Scene detail — walls, wall types, RF materials, doors, windows, and obstructions per floor
• Radio inventory — every access point, DAS remote unit, and antenna, with model, band,
  transmit power, height, and placement
• Coverage statistics — RSRP, RSSI, RSRQ, SINR, throughput, and Wi-Fi SNR distributions
  with percent-of-area covered, computed from your saved simulations
• Capacity — offered demand, per-cell load, and where a design falls short
• Design-criteria compliance — each KPI checked against the threshold your design profile
  sets, per network and band, with p5–p95 percentiles showing how far a shortfall falls,
  plus cable-length budget violations
• Bill of materials — parts, quantities, and part numbers
• Point-to-multipoint link data for fixed-wireless designs
• Generated reports — list them and retrieve their contents

Every tool is read-only. The connector cannot create, modify, or delete projects, designs,
reports, or simulation settings, and it never triggers a new simulation — coverage and
capacity figures come from results you have already generated.

Requires an eino account. Sign in with your normal eino credentials when you connect.

_published_faq.name: How do I add eino to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add eino to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://mcp.eino.ai/. This server requires OAuth, so complete the login prompt after you connect.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the eino MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: eino provides these MCP tools: get_bom, get_capacity_summary, get_coverage_stats, get_pmp_data, get_portfolio_summary, get_project_overview, get_radio_inventory, get_report, get_scene_summary, and list_reports.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to eino?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to eino in productivity on the Manufact MCP catalog include Autodesk Product Help, BoardWise, FlagStat, Keenable Web Search, and PomoDial.
eino requires authentication. Connect it in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor and complete the OAuth login prompt.
eino is developed by eino.ai. It is listed as community on the Claude connector directory.
